title: Market data
description: The market data platform: holiday calendars (calendar-svc's golden calendars, since phase 2), Treasury CMT yields (quote-svc's golden quotes and freshness, mkt-data's near-raw observations), capture history from mkt-data's sources, storage from postgres-exporter and the cost-exporter.

panels.title: Database reachable
panels.description: mkt-data could read its database for this scrape (mkt_data_db_up).

panels.title: Parse failures
panels.description: Sources whose latest parse failed. The 'Market data parse failed' alert fires on these; home-mcp mkt_data_checks shows the error.

panels.title: Oldest successful fetch
panels.description: Longest time since any source was last fetched or read successfully. The weekly DAGs keep this under 7 days; the stale alert fires past that.

panels.title: Coverage gaps
panels.description: Years inside each calendar's covered range that no source covers.

panels.title: Next year published
panels.description: Whether next year is covered by a publisher (not rules or a projection). Overdue only from each calendar's usual publish date (SIFMA-US: Dec 20).

panels.title: Upcoming closes and early closes (next 180 days)
panels.description: Every full close and early close in the next 180 days, soonest first. Times are Eastern. Projected rows come from rules in years no publisher has posted yet.

panels.title: Coverage per calendar and kind of source
panels.description: Which years each kind of source covers: published (a publisher's page or file), rules (cited rule sets for older years) and projected (rules forward to 2100, full closes only). A year counts once, for its highest-precedence source.

panels.title: Gaps and stored days per calendar
panels.description: Uncovered years inside each calendar's range (gap years are listed by calendar_svc_calendar_gap_year), and the current closed and early-close weekdays stored.

panels.title: Sources
panels.description: Each source in precedence order within its calendar: when it was last fetched (or read) successfully, whether its latest parse worked, and the raw captures kept. An unchanged fetch records a check, not a capture.

panels.title: Raw captures kept, by source
panels.description: Capture history: a step up is a new capture (the publisher's content changed). Raw captures are never deleted.

panels.title: Time since last successful fetch, by source
panels.description: Resets to zero on every successful run. The weekly DAGs make a sawtooth below 7 days.

panels.title: Curve due
panels.description: The latest SIFMA-US business day whose Treasury curve is due (by 9:00 a.m. New York the next day), from quote-svc with calendar-svc's closes.

panels.title: Missing the due curve
panels.description: Active instruments with no Treasury (UST-PAR) value for the due date. Alert: Treasury curve missing.

panels.title: Source disagreements
panels.description: Dates where Treasury and H.15 give different values (they should be identical). Alert: Treasury sources disagree.

panels.title: Revisions
panels.description: Quote values Treasury or the Fed changed after publishing, kept in quote-svc's history (info only).

panels.title: Last quote load
panels.description: Time since quote-svc's last successful load (on every new capture, plus nightly). Alert after 30 hours.

panels.title: Unmapped keys
panels.description: Source keys secmaster-svc has no instrument for: their values aren't loaded (a new tenor, say).

panels.title: Instruments
panels.description: Per instrument: latest Treasury date and whether it's missing for the due date; golden first and last date and values; business days golden is missing against the bond calendar (SIFMA-US from 1996, the Fed's 1986-1995, weekdays before); how many latest golden yields in a row are identical (a stuck feed repeats).

panels.title: Ingestion: latest date per source key
panels.description: mkt-data's near-raw observations: each Treasury (UST-PAR) and H.15 (H15-TCM) key's latest date with a value, from the source's newest month. H.15 runs a business day behind Treasury.

panels.title: Longest gaps in golden
panels.description: Runs of business days golden has no value for (the longest 20 per instrument): the 20-year 1987-1993 and 30-year 2002-2006 gaps are real; one- or two-day gaps before 1996 are bond-market closes the Fed's calendar doesn't mark (docs/phase-2.md, B6).

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: The market data platform's Postgres databases together: mkt-data, calendar-svc, secmaster-svc and quote-svc (postgres-exporter).

panels.title: Raw captures
panels.description: Bytes of raw captures stored, all sources.

panels.title: Calendar rows
panels.description: Current closed and early-close weekdays, all calendars.

panels.title: AWS month to date
panels.description: The whole AWS account, not just market data (cost-exporter; Cost Explorer lags about a day).

panels.title: AWS forecast this month
panels.description: Cost Explorer's forecast for the month, whole account. Budget is about $200/month.

panels.title: Storage over time
panels.description: Database size and raw capture bytes.
